key_highlights: Headline CPI rose to 4.3%, locking in market expectations for a fifth RBA rate hike next week.
ASX closed flat as mining gains counterbalanced broad declines in banking and retail.
Energy sector split: coal rallies on wartime demand while gas faces regulatory and ESG hurdles.
Tech showed resilience via Anthropic IPO interest, despite the collapsed Firmus data centre float.

sectors.trend: Large-cap miners advanced despite volatile iron ore; BlueScope surged on US tariff protections while junior gold and critical minerals reported strong operational progress.
sectors.implications: Overweight tariff-hedged steel and low-cost gold producers; maintain selective exposure to bulk iron ore miners.

sectors.trend: Major banks retreated as sticky 4.3% inflation amplified expectations of another RBA rate hike, heightening mortgage stress concerns.
sectors.implications: Underweight major banks due to net interest margin compression and downside risk in overstretched housing markets.

sectors.trend: War-driven demand lifted coal equities, while major domestic gas producers faced environmental challenges and regulator scrutiny.
sectors.implications: Favor export coal producers for cash generation; monitor project approval delays for Woodside and Santos.

sectors.trend: Tech equities rallied tracking global sentiment and Anthropic IPO momentum, though local AI data centre investments were clouded by Firmus float withdrawal.
sectors.implications: Prefer proven software providers over uncontracted capital-intensive AI infrastructure plays.

sectors.trend: Discretionary retailers sold off on rate hike fears, while Star Entertainment jumped after absorbing a $260m regulatory penalty.
sectors.implications: Rotate toward defensive consumer staples and avoid consumer discretionary stocks vulnerable to household budget tightening.

sectors.trend: Yield-sensitive property trusts face renewed pressure from higher bond yields and regional housing market strains.
sectors.implications: Underweight high-gearing REITs exposed to secondary commercial assets and softening residential developments.

key_themes: Accelerating CPI to 4.3% cements an RBA cash rate hike at next week's Melbourne Cup meeting.
Rotation out of interest-rate sensitive financials and consumer retail into resources and defensive earners.
Global trade tariffs and geopolitical conflicts creating clear winners (steel, coal) and losers.
AI infrastructure enthusiasm facing reality check regarding capital requirements and execution.

risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight high-multiple and debt-dependent equities; shift toward cash and short-duration fixed interest.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Regulatory and ESG Impediments on Gas Projects
risk_assessment.mitigation: Trim exposure to offshore exploration with pending environmental approvals.
Focus on established tech balance sheets rather than speculative infrastructure floats.
Limit exposure to regional residential developers and mortgage-heavy regional lenders.

opportunities.rationale: Direct earnings upside from US steel tariffs via North Star business.

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical allocation to thermal and coking coal producers
opportunities.rationale: Geopolitical conflict continues to support global seaborne prices and strong cash flow generation.

opportunities.recommendation: Accumulate low-cost gold and critical minerals developers
opportunities.rationale: High-grade exploration intercepts and strategic supply chain diversification provide strong fundamentals.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim exposure to Big Four Australian Banks
defensive_moves.rationale: Impending RBA rate hike increases credit impairment risks and caps mortgage lending expansion.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce holdings in Discretionary Retail and Conglomerates
defensive_moves.rationale: Elevated inflation and borrowing costs will crimp household disposable income.
Elevated local bond yields and RBA tightening pose downside valuation risks to the broader index.

market_outlook.short_term: Range-bound ASX 200 with downward pressure leading into next week's RBA Melbourne Cup meeting following the 4.3% CPI print.
market_outlook.long_term: Widening performance dispersion favoring resource exporters and tariff-insulated cyclicals over domestic interest-rate sensitive sectors.
key_catalysts: RBA Melbourne Cup Day cash rate decision
US FOMC follow-through and US Treasury yield trajectory
Regulatory approvals updates for Santos and Woodside projects
watch_list: AUD/USD exchange rate behavior around RBA hike
Iron ore 62% Fe CFR Qingdao benchmark and seaborne thermal coal prices
Bank mortgage arrears and credit impairment updates
